papers.title: A Generalizable Multimodal Model for Treatment-Stratified Risk and Survival Assessment under Real-World Constraints: A Multi-Center Study of Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Integrating histopathology, genomic, and clinical phenotypes holds promise for improving prognostic patient stratification, including within treatment-defined subgroups, in colorectal cancer (CRC). However, ensuring the availability of all modalities in routine clinical practice remains challenging. Comprehensive molecular profiling is often constrained by cost and turnaround time, leaving histopathology as the most consistently available modality across institutions. In addition, variability in staining protocols, scanning devices, patient demographics, and outcome distributions across center
papers.summary: This multi-center study develops a multimodal machine learning model that integrates histopathology, genomics, and clinical data to stratify colorectal cancer patients by treatment and predict survival, while addressing real-world constraints like missing modalities. The model is designed to remain robust when only histopathology is available, making it more generalizable across institutions with varying resources and protocols.

papers.title: Post-Search Validation and Curation of Site-Resolved N‑Glycoproteomics Data.
papers.abstract: Given the significant role of glycosylation in modulating protein structure and activity, glycoproteomics is gaining increased interest from the broad scientific community. Large-scale site-resolved N-glycoproteomics relies on automated MS2-based searches, but candidate glycopeptide assignments can remain ambiguous when isomeric or isobaric glycan structures, adducts, chemical modifications, in-source fragments, or incomplete MS2 evidence support more than one plausible interpretation. Here, we systematically categorize common challenges and misassignments in glycoproteomics and present a post
papers.summary: This paper systematically catalogs common challenges and misassignments that arise in large-scale site-resolved N-glycoproteomics when automated MS2-based searches produce ambiguous glycopeptide assignments. It presents a post-search validation and curation framework to help researchers distinguish correct assignments from artifacts caused by isomeric/isobaric glycans, adducts, modifications, and incomplete MS2 evidence.

papers.title: Enhanced Sampling of Protein Conformations in AlphaFold3 with Repulsive Bias in the Diffusion Generative Model.
papers.abstract: Conformational changes in proteins are vital to their function yet remain challenging for state-of-the-art artificial intelligence, such as AlphaFold3 (AF3), to predict. It has been observed that AF3 sometimes fails to capture ligand-induced conformational changes, even though it explicitly includes ligand molecules that induce such changes. To address this challenge, we develop an enhanced sampling scheme that leverages the diffusion-based generative model used in AF3 to predict protein structures. Interpreting the diffusion generative model as a stochastic sampling process analogous to molec
papers.summary: The authors introduce an enhanced sampling method that adds a repulsive bias to AlphaFold3's diffusion-based structure prediction, allowing it to explore alternative protein conformations rather than collapsing to a single predicted state. This addresses AF3's known limitation in capturing ligand-induced conformational changes, even when the ligand is explicitly provided. The approach draws an analogy between AF3's diffusion process and molecular dynamics sampling to broaden conformational coverage.

papers.title: Development and validation of a multimodal MRI habitat-based deep learning fusion model for predicting 252Cf neutron therapy response in cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide. Although californium-252 (252Cf) neutron brachytherapy has demonstrated favorable therapeutic efficacy for locally advanced cervical cancer, substantial inter-patient heterogeneity in treatment response still exists. Therefore, developing a reliable non-invasive predictive model before treatment is of considerable clinical importance.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates a deep learning fusion model that combines multimodal MRI-based tumor habitat imaging to predict how cervical cancer patients will respond to californium-252 neutron brachytherapy. The goal is to provide a non-invasive, pre-treatment tool for stratifying patients and guiding clinical decisions in locally advanced cervical cancer.

papers.title: Attribution assignment for deep-generative sequence models enables interpretability analysis using positive-only data.
papers.abstract: Generative machine learning models offer a powerful framework for therapeutic design, by efficiently exploring large spaces of biological sequences enriched for desirable properties. Unlike supervised learning methods, which require both positive and negative labeled data, generative models such as LSTMs can be trained solely on positively labeled sequences, for example, high-affinity antibodies. This is particularly advantageous in biological settings where negative data are scarce, unreliable, or biologically ill-defined. However, the lack of attribution methods for generative models has hin
papers.summary: The authors introduce an attribution method for deep generative sequence models (like LSTMs) that were trained only on positive examples, such as high-affinity antibodies. This allows researchers to identify which parts of a generated sequence contribute to its desirable properties without needing negative training data. The approach improves interpretability of generative models in therapeutic design where negative data are scarce or unreliable.

papers.title: Lipid tail length dictates membrane disruption by carmofur analogs and reveals noncanonical modes of action.
papers.abstract: Carmofur, a lipidated urethane derivative and prodrug of 5-fluorouracil, has an established clinical application as an antineoplastic agent for the treatment of colorectal cancer, primarily through inhibition of acid ceramidase and subsequent intracellular drug release. Beyond this oncological application, recent drug repurposing efforts have identified covalent inhibition of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease as an additional antiviral mechanism. The pronounced amphiphilic character of carmofur, arising from a polar fluoropyrimidine headgroup appended to a hydrophobic aliphatic tail, raises the pos
papers.summary: This study investigates how the length of the lipid tail in carmofur analogs affects their ability to disrupt membranes, revealing that tail length is a key determinant of membrane activity. The findings suggest that carmofur and its analogs may act through noncanonical mechanisms beyond their known targets, such as acid ceramidase and SARS-CoV-2 main protease. This work provides insight into the structure-activity relationships of amphiphilic drugs and their membrane interactions.

papers.title: Predicting Enzyme Turnover Numbers and Enabling Rational Enzyme Evolution.
papers.abstract: Enzyme turnover number ( k cat  ) is a central kinetic parameter for biocatalysis, but experimental determination is low-throughput and existing computational methods inadequately model enzyme-reaction interplay. Here, we introduced MCKcat, a deep learning framework that integrates multi-scale convolutional feature extraction and cross-attention to enable deep, reciprocal fusion of enzyme sequence and reaction fingerprint representations for accurate k cat  prediction. We constructed MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset comprising 33 396 enzyme-reaction-based k cat  data points, covering both wild
papers.summary: The authors developed MCKcat, a deep learning framework that combines multi-scale convolutional feature extraction with cross-attention to jointly model enzyme sequences and reaction fingerprints for predicting enzyme turnover numbers (kcat). They also built MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset of 33,396 enzyme-reaction kcat data points, and demonstrated its utility for rational enzyme evolution. This addresses a key bottleneck in biocatalysis where experimental kcat measurement is low-throughput and existing computational methods poorly capture enzyme-reaction interplay.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Multitask Framework Integrating Habitat and Deep Learning for Predicting Early Disease Control and Survival in Immunotherapy-Treated Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients show heterogeneous responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This study developed ECOS-Net, a transformer-based multitask network integrating CT-derived habitat and 2.5-dimensional (2.5D) deep learning features for simultaneously predicting early disease control (DC) and overall survival (OS). Of 1,234 patients with HCC enrolled from eight institutions and public databases, 832 ICI-treated patients were used for model development. ECOS-Net fused features using multi-head attention and generated early DC probabilities and OS risk scores. ECOS-DC a
papers.summary: This study introduces ECOS-Net, a transformer-based multitask deep learning framework that combines CT-derived habitat imaging features with 2.5D deep learning to simultaneously predict early disease control and overall survival in hepatocellular carcinoma patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors. Trained on 832 ICI-treated patients from eight institutions and public databases, the model aims to address heterogeneous treatment responses by providing integrated imaging-based predictions.

papers.title: SpaCEy links spatial tissue patterns to clinical outcomes using explainable graph neural networks.
papers.abstract: Tissues are complex ecosystems organised in space, and alterations in this organisation underpin multiple diseases. Spatial omics enables molecular profiling of tissue organisation, but linking these patterns to clinical outcomes remains challenging. We present SpaCEy (Spatial Clinical Explainability), an explainable graph neural network that identifies tissue patterns predictive of clinical outcomes in spatial proteomics datasets. SpaCEy models tissues as spatial graphs from molecular marker expression, without using predefined cell-type labels or anatomical regions as model inputs. Its embed
papers.summary: SpaCEy is an explainable graph neural network that models spatial proteomics data as graphs built directly from molecular marker expression, avoiding reliance on predefined cell-type labels or anatomical annotations. It identifies spatial tissue patterns that predict clinical outcomes and provides interpretable explanations for those predictions. This offers a general framework for linking tissue organization to clinical endpoints in spatial omics studies.

papers.title: ASAS-NANP SYMPOSIUM: MATHEMATICAL MODELING IN ANIMAL NUTRITION: The Evolution of Large Language Models and Their Impact on Animal Sciences.
papers.abstract: The rapid rise of large language models (LLM) is reshaping the scientific landscape, transitioning from early statistical language models to advanced transformer-based architectures capable of synthesizing knowledge across disciplines. While their predictive capacity and scalability have opened new avenues in data analysis, hypothesis generation, and decision support, concerns remain regarding bias, hallucination, reproducibility, and ethical governance. In animal sciences, LLM are gradually applied to challenges in nutrition modeling, animal health, genetic selection, and sustainability. Prec
papers.summary: This symposium paper reviews the evolution of large language models from early statistical approaches to modern transformer architectures and discusses their emerging applications in animal sciences, including nutrition modeling, animal health, genetic selection, and sustainability. It also highlights key concerns such as bias, hallucination, reproducibility, and ethical governance that must be addressed for responsible adoption.

papers.title: DesignMaster: A Multi-Conditional Diffusion Framework for Rational PROTAC Design.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable targeted protein degradation through ternary complex formation with E3 ubiquitin ligase. However, the rational design of PROTACs remains highly challenging due to limited structure-activity relationship data and the vast conformational diversity of linkers. Existing computational approaches can be broadly divided into structure-based ternary modelling methods and fragment-based linker generation models. Although these approaches have advanced PROTAC design, they typically neglect key physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during th
papers.summary: DesignMaster introduces a multi-conditional diffusion framework for the rational design of PROTAC molecules, which are bifunctional compounds that degrade target proteins via the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Unlike prior structure-based or fragment-based methods, it incorporates physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during generation, aiming to produce more synthesizable and effective degraders. This addresses a key bottleneck in PROTAC development where linker design and drug-like properties are often poorly controlled.

papers.title: Learning Protein-Protein Binding Free Energies from Interface Graphs and Physicochemical Descriptors.
papers.abstract: Predicting protein-protein binding free energy (ΔG) from structure remains a central challenge in computational biophysics. Here, we present GULP (Graph-based Unified Learning for Protein binding), a graph neural network (GNN) that jointly learns from a residue-level graph representation of the binding interface and global physicochemical descriptors. We systematically investigate how training data distribution affects model performance by comparing a full training set with a balanced subset enriched for extreme-affinity complexes. GULP is computationally efficient and provides interpretable i
papers.summary: GULP is a graph neural network that predicts protein-protein binding free energy by combining a residue-level graph representation of the binding interface with global physicochemical descriptors. The authors show that training data distribution, particularly enrichment for extreme-affinity complexes, affects model performance, and the model is computationally efficient and interpretable.

papers.title: Portable near-infrared spectroscopy combined with machine learning for rapid detection of broiler breast myopathies.
papers.abstract: Growth-related breast myopathies are among the major meat quality defects encountered in modern broiler production, affecting breast meat quality and requiring affected fillets to be diverted to further processing. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of a pocket-sized near‑infrared (NIR) spectrometer for detecting white striping (WS), wooden breast (WB), and spaghetti meat (SM) in broiler breast meat. A total of 4579 broilers from a commercial crossbred and a broiler breeders line were sampled across 8 flocks and multiple slaughter days, and fillets were categorized by a trained evalu
papers.summary: This study tested whether a pocket-sized near-infrared spectrometer combined with machine learning could detect common broiler breast muscle defects (white striping, wooden breast, and spaghetti meat) in a large sample of 4,579 broilers across multiple flocks and slaughter days. The approach aims to provide a rapid, portable, non-destructive method for classifying affected fillets on the processing line.

papers.title: Integrated Systems Toxicology Analysis and Molecular Dynamics Study Reveal the Potential Mechanism by which Benzo[a]pyrene Contributes to Depression in Lung Adenocarcinoma via RNASE1 Upregulation.
papers.abstract: Benzo-[a]-pyrene (Bap), a prominent carcinogen found in tobacco smoke and air pollution, is closely associated with lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and subsequent depression, though the mechanism underlying this comorbidity remains unclear. LUAD patients were categorized based on depression-related gene expression. Prognostic genes identified through machine learning were cross-referenced with predicted Bap targets. Mendelian randomization (MR) evaluated the causal relationship between RNASE1 and depression. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), molecular docking, and 100 ns molecular dynamics (M
papers.summary: This study integrates systems toxicology, machine learning, and Mendelian randomization to show that benzo[a]pyrene exposure may promote depression in lung adenocarcinoma patients through upregulation of RNASE1. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations support RNASE1 as a mechanistic link between the carcinogen and depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Chemically Informed Machine Learning Approach for Prediction of Reactivity Ratios in Radical Copolymerization.
papers.abstract: Predicting monomer reactivity ratios is crucial for controlling monomer sequence distribution in copolymers and their properties. Traditional experimental methods of determining reactivity ratios are time-consuming and resource-intensive, while existing computational methods often struggle with accuracy or scalability. Here, we present a method that combines unsupervised learning with artificial neural networks to predict reactivity ratios in radical copolymerization. By applying spectral clustering to physicochemical features of monomers, we identified three distinct monomer groups with chara
papers.summary: This paper introduces a machine learning method that combines spectral clustering of monomer physicochemical features with artificial neural networks to predict reactivity ratios in radical copolymerization. The approach aims to overcome the time and resource demands of experimental determination and the accuracy/scalability limits of existing computational methods.

papers.title: HD-AIP: A Heterogeneous Dual-Stream Alignment-Free Framework for Anti-Inflammatory Peptide Prediction Based on Language Models and CT-Net.
papers.abstract: Anti-inflammatory peptides (AIPs) show therapeutic potential for treating chronic and autoimmune diseases. Computational screening of these peptides remains challenging because their typically short sequences limit traditional feature extraction effectiveness, while homology-based methods incur high computational costs.
papers.summary: The authors present HD-AIP, a computational framework for predicting anti-inflammatory peptides that avoids sequence alignment by combining protein language models with a CT-Net architecture in a dual-stream design. This alignment-free approach addresses the difficulty of extracting features from short peptide sequences and the high computational cost of homology-based methods.

papers.title: Combined Analysis of Transcriptome and Metabolome of Large-Size Triploid Rainbow Trout in Different Seasons.
papers.abstract: Seasonal temperature variation poses a significant physiological challenge for cold-water aquaculture species; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying seasonal adaptation in large-sized triploid rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) remain largely unexplored. In this study, we integrated liver transcriptomics and LC-MS-based untargeted metabolomics across four seasons (February, May, August, November) to investigate this phenomenon. Seasonal comparisons revealed pronounced molecular reprogramming, with the comparison between May and August showing the largest transcriptomic shift (13,359 di
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study integrated liver transcriptomics and untargeted metabolomics in large triploid rainbow trout across four seasons to uncover molecular mechanisms of seasonal adaptation. The May-to-August transition showed the largest transcriptomic shift, revealing pronounced seasonal molecular reprogramming in this cold-water aquaculture species.

papers.title: A reference genome without a virus: cDNA reconstruction reveals the provenance and function of the MS2 phage sequence.
papers.abstract: Reference genomes are often treated as faithful representations of experimentally validated viral genomes, yet the relationship between historically curated reference sequences and infectivity is rarely tested experimentally. Here, we developed a cDNA-based reconstruction platform for the canonical RNA phage MS2 and used it to compare the current NCBI reference genome (RefSeq) with closely related published isolate sequences. We found that isolate-derived sequences reproducibly yielded infectious phage, whereas the current MS2 RefSeq-derived construct did not, showing that the present referenc
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed a cDNA-based reconstruction platform for the RNA phage MS2 and found that the current NCBI RefSeq reference genome does not produce infectious phage, while closely related published isolate sequences do. This reveals that the curated reference sequence has lost infectivity, likely due to historical errors or accumulated changes, and highlights the need to experimentally validate reference genomes.

papers.title: ProtThermoRank: Sequence-based multi-class prediction model for protein thermal stability changes and its application to CcsZ.
papers.abstract: Protein thermal stability is a key property of industrial enzymes and biopharmaceutical proteins. The rapid and accurate evaluation of thermal stability across large numbers of variants has become a critical step in protein engineering. However, experimental screening of large mutational landscapes remains time-consuming, labor-intensive, and costly. Here, we present ProtThermoRank, a sequence-based multiclass prediction model for mutation-induced changes in protein thermal stability. Unlike existing approaches that encode reference and mutant sequences independently, ProtThermoRank explicitly
papers.summary: ProtThermoRank is a sequence-based model that predicts mutation-induced changes in protein thermal stability as a multi-class problem, distinguishing it from prior binary or regression approaches. Unlike existing methods that encode reference and mutant sequences independently, it explicitly captures the relationship between them, enabling rapid screening of large mutational landscapes. The authors demonstrate its utility by applying it to the protein CcsZ.

papers.title: Mapping Gene Expression to an Interpretable Semantic Space.
papers.abstract: Cell embeddings organize single-cell expression data, but their dimensions have no biological meaning, so clusters are interpreted afterward. We present MESIC (Mapping Expression to Semantic space with Interpretable Components), which builds the written knowledge about genes held in curated databases into the dimensions themselves. A biomedical language model converts each gene's summary into a semantic embedding. MESIC compresses these embeddings into a small number of components, each concentrated on a small set of genes and explained by their annotations. The components are computed once fr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: MESIC is a new method that builds single-cell embeddings whose dimensions are directly interpretable by using a biomedical language model to encode gene summaries from curated databases. Each component is concentrated on a small set of genes and can be explained by their annotations, so clusters don't need post-hoc interpretation. The components are computed once and can be reused across datasets.

papers.title: VirPLM: Antigenic prediction of influenza A/H3N2 viruses with a fine-tuned protein language model.
papers.abstract: Human influenza A/H3N2 viruses undergo rapid antigenic evolution primarily driven by the hemagglutinin subunit 1 (HA1). Within HA1, amino acid substitutions under immune pressure cause antigenic drift, necessitating frequent updates to vaccine strains. While hemagglutination inhibition (HI) assays remain the gold standard for assessing antigenic relationships, their labor-intensive and low-throughput nature limits scalability. Fortunately, the rapid accumulation of HA1 sequences enables sequence-based antigenic prediction, yet effectively extracting informative representations from these viral
papers.summary: The authors developed VirPLM, a fine-tuned protein language model that predicts antigenic relationships between influenza A/H3N2 strains directly from hemagglutinin HA1 sequences. This offers a scalable, sequence-based alternative to labor-intensive hemagglutination inhibition assays, which are the current gold standard for antigenic characterization. The approach could help anticipate antigenic drift and inform more timely vaccine strain selection.

papers.title: Regulatory-prior-guided attention preserves biological structure during unpaired single-cell RNA-ATAC integration.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing and single-cell ATAC sequencing provide complementary views of transcriptional output and chromatin regulatory potential, but integrating unpaired profiles remains challenging because the modalities differ in feature space, sparsity and noise. Existing approaches often frame integration as distribution matching, which can over-align biologically distinct, condition-specific or modality-specific cell states. We present scHPGT, a single-cell Heterogeneous Prior-Guided Transformer for regulatory-prior-guided integration of unpaired RNA and chromatin accessibility profil
papers.summary: The paper introduces scHPGT, a transformer-based method that integrates unpaired single-cell RNA and ATAC profiles using regulatory priors to guide alignment. Unlike distribution-matching approaches that can over-align biologically distinct cell states, scHPGT preserves biological structure while bridging the two modalities. This offers a more faithful integration of transcriptomic and epigenomic single-cell data.

papers.title: Bridging Nano-Interface Interactions and Organ-Specific Toxicity: A Review of Machine Learning for Nanomaterials Risk Assessment.
papers.abstract: Risk assessment of engineered nanomaterials (ENMs) is essential for protecting human health and the environment. Traditional hazard assessments rely primarily on in vivo testing, which faces technical challenges in extrapolation validity, ethical dilemmas, and high costs. Machine learning (ML) models offer alternative approaches that are aligned with the 3R principles (Replacement, Reduction, and Refinement) for reducing animal use. ML methods help address the economic, ethical, and temporal limitations of traditional nanotoxicology while advancing mechanistic understanding. This review presen
papers.summary: This review examines how machine learning models can predict the toxicity of engineered nanomaterials, offering an alternative to traditional animal-based testing that aligns with 3R principles. It highlights how ML approaches address cost, ethical, and time limitations in nanotoxicology while also advancing mechanistic understanding of nano-interface interactions and organ-specific toxicity.

papers.title: HERA: Bioinspired Separation of Local Fault Response and Language-Model Scheduling in Simulated Quadruped Control.
papers.abstract: Language-model inference can delay emergency supervision, but cancellation alone cannot provide an immediate physical response. HERA (Hierarchical Event-driven Reflex Architecture) separates a measurement-driven deterministic local action from language-service scheduling, with biological inspiration limited to temporal separation and local feedback. A fixed 1472-trial campaign evaluated canonical-command scheduling, simulated actuator faults and live integration. Across three workloads, the mean validated-command latency was 0.486-0.512 s with preemption, 1.476-11.101 s with single-lane FIFO a
papers.summary: HERA is a control architecture for simulated quadruped robots that separates fast, deterministic local reflex responses from slower language-model-based scheduling, inspired by biological temporal separation. In a 1472-trial campaign, it achieved validated-command latencies of 0.486–0.512 s with preemption versus 1.476–11.101 s with single-lane FIFO scheduling, showing that local fault responses can act immediately while language services handle higher-level scheduling.

papers.title: 3D Spatial Interactomics Maps the Dynamics of NF-κB Multiprotein Signalosomes in Single Cells.
papers.abstract: NFκB signaling drives inflammatory responses by rapidly assembling membrane-proximal multiprotein supercomplexes, yet how these assemblies are organized in space and time within the 3D interior of a single cell has remained uncharacterized. We addressed this by profiling endogenous NFκB protein-protein interactions with an intelligent sequential proximity ligation assay (iseqPLA), read out by spinning disk confocal microscopy and 3D reconstruction. Each detected protein-protein proximity event is represented by a rolling-circle amplification product, and we treat clusters of co-localized punct
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed iseqPLA, a sequential proximity ligation assay combined with 3D confocal microscopy, to map endogenous NF-κB protein-protein interactions in single cells. They show that NF-κB signaling involves dynamic, spatially organized multiprotein signalosomes at the membrane, revealing new details about how these complexes assemble in 3D space and time.

papers.title: An open benchmark and language models for AI in aging biology.
papers.abstract: Over the past two decades, human aging has been characterized across DNA methylation, transcriptomic, proteomic, and clinical modalities, yet no benchmark evaluates whether AI systems can interpret these heterogeneous data types in the context of aging biology. We introduce LongevityBench, an open suite of 17 tasks spanning five biodata domains, and use it to assess 18 frontier AI systems from six developer teams. Despite recent advances in AI, no single model dominates all tasks, with omics-based age prediction being the hardest task regardless of scale. To test whether these gaps can be clos
papers.summary: The authors introduce LongevityBench, an open benchmark of 17 tasks across five biodata domains for evaluating AI systems on aging biology, and use it to assess 18 frontier AI models. They find that no single model excels across all tasks, with omics-based age prediction proving the hardest regardless of model scale, and they develop language models to address these gaps.

papers.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Cell Types in Describing Neuronal Physiological Features.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) captures detailed gene expression profiles at scale, while patch-clamp recordings measure intrinsic neuronal electrophysiological properties. Modeling the relations between these two modalities remains a challenge. Here, we compare how well electrophysiological features can be predicted by traditional transcriptomic cell type classification, representations derived from a foundational model (scGPT) pretrained on large-scale scRNA-seq datasets, ion channel-coding genes, and highly variable genes. Using paired transcriptomic and electrophysiological patch-s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint compares how well different transcriptomic representations predict neuronal electrophysiological properties from paired patch-clamp and scRNA-seq data. Surprisingly, traditional cell type classifications outperform both scGPT foundation model embeddings and ion channel gene expression in predicting physiological features. The results suggest that discrete cell type labels remain a highly effective, simple descriptor of neuronal physiology.

papers.title: MAPA: A Semantic Network Framework for Functional Module Discovery and Interpretation in Multi-Omics Data.
papers.abstract: Multi-omics technologies generate high-dimensional molecular signatures that provide unprecedented opportunities to uncover biological mechanisms. However, translating complex molecular alterations into coherent and interpretable functional insights remains a major challenge. Existing module discovery methods can identify groups of related features, but often lack direct biological interpretability, whereas pathway-based approaches frequently yield redundant results that complicate interpretation. Here, we present MAPA (Modular Analysis and Phenotype-informed Annotation using large language mo
papers.summary: MAPA is a semantic network framework that discovers and interprets functional modules in multi-omics data by combining module discovery with large language model-based phenotype-informed annotation. It aims to overcome the limited biological interpretability of existing module discovery methods and the redundancy of pathway-based approaches. The tool is designed to help translate complex molecular alterations into coherent, interpretable functional insights.

papers.title: Genolator enables protein function interpretation using a multimodal large language model fusing genomic and structural interpretation with natural language interaction.
papers.abstract: Decoding the genetic code to unveil its genome functionality is a monumental task which would greatly advance the understanding of disease mechanisms and development of targeted treatments. Although large language models (LLMs) have transformed natural language processing across diverse domains, translating the complex language of DNA into human-readable form remains challenging due to genomic data complexity and unexplored regions of the human genome. Current language models either are capable of processing natural language or the genomic code. Models fusing both aspects are largely lacking.
papers.summary: Genolator is a multimodal large language model that integrates genomic sequence data with protein structural information and natural language interaction to interpret protein function. It addresses the gap in existing models that handle either natural language or genomic code but not both, aiming to make DNA-level information human-readable for disease and drug research.

papers.title: BAN-SDBPred: Improving Single-Stranded and Double-Stranded DNA-Binding Protein Prediction Using an Attention Network with Bilinear Convolution and Adaptive Sampling Strategy.
papers.abstract: DNA binding proteins play essential roles in numerous biological mechanisms. The DBPs can be either single-stranded binding (SSBs) or double-stranded binding (DSBs) to a DNA molecule. The in-depth identification of SSBs and DSBs has been a hot topic in bioinformatics and is involved in the drug discovery process. Traditional experimental methods failed to characterize the types of DBPs because of high cost and time constraints. While computational prediction of novel SSBs and DSBs has made significant progress, there are still challenges remaining in enhancing overall prediction performance. M
papers.summary: BAN-SDBPred is a computational tool that predicts whether a DNA-binding protein interacts with single-stranded or double-stranded DNA. It combines an attention network with bilinear convolution and an adaptive sampling strategy to improve prediction accuracy over existing methods. This could aid drug discovery and functional annotation of DNA-binding proteins without costly experiments.

papers.title: miRAssist: a context-aware, evidence integration framework for interpretable miRNA-target prioritization.
papers.abstract: MicroRNA-target interaction prediction remains challenging because many existing tools provide prediction scores or ranked candidate lists without making the supporting evidence easy to interpret or relate to a specific biological context.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: miRAssist is a new computational framework that predicts microRNA-target interactions by integrating multiple lines of evidence in a context-aware manner. Unlike existing tools that output opaque scores or ranked lists, it aims to make the supporting evidence interpretable and tied to specific biological contexts. This addresses a key bottleneck in miRNA research where predictions are hard to trust or validate.

papers.title: Retrieval-Guided Transfer Learning for Low-Resource Ebola Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction plays an important role in computational drug discovery; however, its application to emerging infectious diseases such as Ebola remains challenging because of the limited availability of experimentally measured affinity data. To address this low-resource setting, we propose a retrieval-guided transfer-learning framework that leverages BindingDB interactions to improve Ebola DTA prediction. The framework uses a two-stage strategy. In Stage I, source interactions are selected using random sampling, compound-similarity retrieval, protein-similarity retrieval,
papers.summary: The authors propose a retrieval-guided transfer-learning framework to predict drug-target binding affinity for Ebola, a disease with very few experimentally measured affinity data. The method first selects relevant source interactions from BindingDB using random sampling and compound/protein similarity retrieval, then transfers this knowledge to improve Ebola DTA prediction. This addresses the practical challenge of building predictive models when target-specific data are scarce.

papers.title: Innovative Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Bacteriophage Research: A New Chapter in Future Medicine.
papers.abstract: As the crisis of antibiotic resistance escalates, phage therapy has regained attention as an alternative strategy. Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies offer new avenues to overcome the bottlenecks inherent in traditional bacteriophage research. This review summarizes the multi-dimensional innovative applications of machine learning, deep learning, and large biological models in phage studies. In the fields of phage recognition and genomics, support vector machines (SVMs), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and pre-trained protein language models can all achieve recognition accuracy ra
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning, deep learning, and large biological models are being applied across bacteriophage research, including phage recognition, genomics, and therapeutic development. It highlights that methods like SVMs, CNNs, and pre-trained protein language models can achieve high accuracy in phage identification. The authors frame these AI tools as key to overcoming bottlenecks in phage therapy amid rising antibiotic resistance.

papers.title: Routine Laboratory-Based Machine Learning for Discriminating Multiple Myeloma from Clinical Mimickers: Development and Internal Validation of a Diagnostic Prediction Model.
papers.abstract: Background: Multiple myeloma (MM) diagnosis requires specialised testing that is not universally available, contributing to diagnostic delays. The aim of this study was to develop and internally validate statistical and machine learning (ML) models that discriminate MM from clinically similar conditions using exclusively routine laboratory parameters. Methods: This retrospective diagnostic prediction model study included 422 consecutive patients referred to hematology for suspected MM at a tertiary care center (2017-2025). Fifteen routine demographic and laboratory variables were used to train
papers.summary: This study developed and internally validated statistical and machine learning models that distinguish multiple myeloma from clinically similar conditions using only routine laboratory and demographic variables. Using data from 422 patients referred for suspected myeloma, the models aim to enable earlier diagnosis in settings lacking specialized testing. The work is a proof-of-concept for routine-lab-based diagnostic prediction.

papers.title: Development of an Interpretable QSAR Model for Predicting Coagulation Factor XIIa Inhibitors Using Ensemble Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Background/Objective: Activated coagulation factor XII (FXIIa) is a component of the contact activation pathway and a pharmacologically relevant target in contact-system-associated processes. In this study, scaffold-aware and interpretable machine-learning QSAR models were developed for human FXIIa activity. Methods: Bioactivity records for the human single protein target CHEMBL2821 were retrieved from ChEMBL release 37. Modeling was restricted to exact IC50 measurements from assays explicitly referring to FXIIa, Factor XIIa, or activated Factor XII. Median-consolidated pIC50 values and two-di
papers.summary: This study developed interpretable machine-learning QSAR models to predict inhibition of coagulation factor XIIa, a target in the contact activation pathway. Using IC50 data from ChEMBL, the authors built ensemble models with scaffold-aware validation and interpretability features. The work provides a predictive tool for identifying FXIIa inhibitors in drug discovery.

papers.title: Biopesticidal Potential of the Cannabis sativa L. Metabolites: A Denoised, Docking-Informed QSAR Model.
papers.abstract: Plant metabolites are a promising source of new biopesticides, but their chemical diversity exceeds the capacity of experimental screening. Cannabis sativa is a particularly attractive crop for discovering such compounds, although its metabolome has not been systematically evaluated for biopesticidal potential. Here, we computationally analyzed 5211 compounds annotated as C. sativa metabolites in the Cannabis Compound Database (CCD) using an integrated framework combining graph-based molecular prediction and protein-ligand interaction analysis. Initial prioritization employed a directed messag
papers.summary: This study computationally screened 5,211 Cannabis sativa metabolites from the Cannabis Compound Database for biopesticidal potential using a docking-informed QSAR model with graph-based molecular prediction. The integrated framework prioritized candidate compounds by combining molecular property prediction with protein-ligand interaction analysis, identifying promising biopesticide leads without experimental screening. The work demonstrates a scalable computational approach to mine plant metabolomes for agrochemical applications.

papers.title: The YTHDF proteins modulate Alzheimer's disease-associated brain gene signatures.
papers.abstract: Gene signatures of Alzheimer's disease (AD) brains reflect the output of a complex interplay of genetic, epigenetic, epi-transcriptomic, and post-transcriptional regulations. To nominate candidate factors modulating these signatures, we developed a machine learning model to integrate cellular and molecular features explaining differential gene expression in AD. Among the features tested, YTHDF proteins, the canonical readers of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification, are among the most influential predictors of AD gene signatures. Protein modules containing YTHDFs were downregulated in huma
papers.summary: This study used a machine learning model to identify factors that explain the gene expression changes seen in Alzheimer's disease brains, finding that YTHDF proteins—the main readers of the m6A RNA modification—are among the strongest predictors. Protein modules containing YTHDFs were downregulated in human AD brains, suggesting these RNA-modifying proteins play a role in shaping AD-associated gene signatures.

papers.title: A Robust Masked Painter Framework for Gene Selection in Binary Classification of High-Dimensional Functional Genomic Data.
papers.abstract: High-dimensional gene expression datasets in chemometric and biomedical research present significant challenges for machine learning because the number of genes greatly exceeds the number of available samples, increasing the risk of overfitting and reducing classification reliability. Existing gene selection methods are often sensitive to noise and outliers, leading to unstable feature subsets and degraded classification performance. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Robust Masked Painter (RMP) framework that integrates robust measures of location and dispersion, namely the M
papers.summary: This paper introduces the Robust Masked Painter (RMP) framework, a gene selection method designed for binary classification of high-dimensional functional genomic data. The approach integrates robust statistical measures of location and dispersion to reduce sensitivity to noise and outliers, aiming to produce more stable feature subsets and improved classification performance compared to existing methods.

papers.title: Evaluating Sequence Foundation Models for Insect Olfactory Gene Discovery: Failure Modes, Evidence Standards, and a Benchmark Agenda.
papers.abstract: Genome-scale searches for insect olfactory genes are vulnerable to rapid receptor divergence, tandem duplication, fragmented gene models, circular labels, and evolutionary leakage between training and test data. Sequence foundation models trained on DNA or proteins may extend homology-based annotation, but available evidence does not support their use as autonomous annotators or direct predictors of sensory function. This critical review organizes the problem around annotation failures rather than model catalogues. We distinguish six inference levels, from candidate locus detection to organism
papers.summary: This critical review argues that sequence foundation models are not yet reliable as autonomous annotators or direct predictors of insect olfactory gene function, due to rapid receptor divergence, tandem duplication, fragmented gene models, circular labels, and evolutionary leakage. It organizes the problem around six inference levels, from candidate locus detection to organism-level function, and proposes evidence standards and a benchmark agenda for evaluating these models.

papers.title: A Systematic Machine Learning Framework for Evaluating and Ranking Omics Layers in Cancer Drug Response Prediction.
papers.abstract: This study introduces a top-down framework for evaluating the utility of multi-omics features to predict the response of 309 drugs in cancer cell lines. This was done by taking a multi-omics approach where data from proteomic, transcriptomic, genomic, metabolomic, and miRNA were integrated with drug sensitivity (area under the curve, AUC) data. We performed modular dimensionality reduction using t-SNE (t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding), followed by K-Means clustering to stratify cell lines into data-driven molecular subgroups, and applied a Random Forest model to refine the drug lis
papers.summary: This study builds a machine learning framework to test how well different omics layers (proteomics, transcriptomics, genomics, metabolomics, miRNA) predict drug response across 309 drugs in cancer cell lines. Using t-SNE dimensionality reduction, K-Means clustering, and Random Forest models, the authors rank which omics data types are most informative for drug response prediction. The work provides a systematic comparison of omics layer utility rather than a new predictive tool.

papers.title: Fast structural search for classification of gut bacterial mucin O-glycan degrading enzymes.
papers.abstract: The Enzyme Commission (EC) numbering scheme provides a hierarchical way to classify enzymes according to their catalytic functions. While recent protein language model (PLM) based approaches like CLEAN and ProteInter have improved sequence-based EC number prediction, they struggle with fine-grained classification at the deepest hierarchical level. Structure-based approaches for grouping similar proteins using alignment tools excel at finding proteins that share overall global structure, but suffer from high false positive rates when classifying proteins that are globally structurally similar b
papers.summary: The authors present a fast structural search method for classifying gut bacterial enzymes that degrade mucin O-glycans, addressing the difficulty of fine-grained EC number prediction at the deepest hierarchical level. Their approach improves on sequence-based protein language model methods and global structural alignment tools, which suffer from high false positive rates for proteins with similar overall folds but different catalytic functions.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven decoding of maternal immune signatures in repeated pregnancy loss.
papers.abstract: Repeated pregnancy loss (RPL) is a multifactorial condition in which the underlying immunological mechanisms, particularly the disruption of maternal-fetal tolerance, remain incompletely understood. Although immune tolerance is critical for pregnancy success, the specific immune dysregulations contributing to RPL, particularly in euploid pregnancies, have been difficult to characterize. To address this, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissues from RPL patients and first-trimester controls. Our analysis initially revealed elevated expression of a transcriptional module of im
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissue from patients with recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) and first-trimester controls to identify immune dysregulation underlying the condition. Machine learning analysis reveals elevated expression of a transcriptional module in immune cells, pointing to disrupted maternal-fetal tolerance as a key mechanism in euploid RPL.

papers.title: Integrating Multimodal MRI Habitat and Transformer-Based Pathomics to Predict High-Risk Molecular Subtypes and Explore Biological Mechanisms in Adult Diffuse Gliomas.
papers.abstract: This study aims to achieve accurate prediction of high-risk molecular subtypes of gliomas through a cross-scale Combined model, matching the model's classification metrics with patient risk stratification and exploring the underlying biological mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study develops a cross-scale combined model that integrates multimodal MRI habitat imaging with transformer-based pathomics to predict high-risk molecular subtypes in adult diffuse gliomas. The model's classification performance is linked to patient risk stratification, and the authors explore the underlying biological mechanisms associated with the predicted subtypes.

papers.title: A Deep-Learning Based Biomarker of Systemic Cellular Senescence Burden to Predict Mortality and Health Outcomes.
papers.abstract: The accumulation of senescent cells is a recognized hallmark of biological aging and is associated with the onset of multiple chronic medical conditions. Senescent cells exhibit a distinct secretory profile, known as the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), which can propagate cellular senescence to neighboring and distant tissues. Measuring SASP factors in blood serves as a practical proxy for cellular senescence burden and may help track disease states and intervention outcomes. We developed and validated a composite SASP Score by integrating large-scale population proteomics da
papers.summary: The authors developed a deep-learning-derived composite SASP Score that integrates large-scale population proteomics data to quantify systemic cellular senescence burden from blood. This biomarker predicts mortality and adverse health outcomes, offering a practical tool for tracking aging-related disease states and intervention effects.

papers.title: ESpma: A method for assessing biological/non-biological interfaces using point-clouds-based structural features and protein language models.
papers.abstract: Distinguishing biological protein-protein interfaces from non-biological contacts remains an important task in structural biology, particularly as protein complex structures continue to accumulate. Recent advances in protein language models (pLMs) have expanded their use across diverse protein prediction tasks, including sequence-based protein-protein interaction prediction. Such approaches often pool representations over entire sequences, whereas structure-based methods commonly rely on more complex graph- or geometry-based integration. We therefore asked how much interface-relevant informati
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: ESpma is a new method that combines point-cloud-based structural features with protein language model embeddings to distinguish biologically meaningful protein-protein interfaces from non-biological crystal contacts. It addresses the gap between sequence-level pLM pooling and complex graph/geometry-based structural methods by integrating both modalities for interface assessment. The approach offers a practical tool for curating the growing number of protein complex structures.

papers.title: Structural and functional perspectives on DEAD-box RNA helicases in the rubber tree cold stress response.
papers.abstract: DExD/H-box RNA helicases constitute one of the largest families of adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-dependent nucleic-acid enzymes, with roles spanning the full breadth of RNA metabolism, from transcription to turnover. Their defining architectural feature is a conserved helicase core comprising two tandem RecA-like domains that couples ATP hydrolysis to duplex unwinding and ribonucleoprotein remodeling. Structural investigations have historically focused on human and yeast model systems, but recent methodological advances, particularly cryo-electron microscopy and deep learning-based structure pr
papers.summary: This review examines DEAD-box RNA helicases in the rubber tree (Hevea brasiliensis), focusing on how their conserved two-domain helicase core couples ATP hydrolysis to RNA unwinding and ribonucleoprotein remodeling during cold stress responses. It highlights recent structural advances from cryo-EM and deep learning-based structure prediction that are extending helicase research beyond traditional human and yeast models into plant systems.

papers.title: Integrative machine learning and transcriptomic analysis reveal a ferroptosis gene signature for pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP) is one of the most common causes of community-acquired pneumonia in children, affecting approximately 10%-40% of pediatric pneumonia cases worldwide. Despite advances in diagnostic and therapeutic approaches, the pathogenesis of severe MPP remains incompletely understood, and patients demonstrate highly heterogeneous responses to treatment. Recent evidence suggests that ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, may play a critical role in the pathophysiology of MPP. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the in
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates machine learning with transcriptomic data to identify a ferroptosis-related gene signature associated with pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP). The authors aim to clarify the molecular mechanisms of severe MPP and address heterogeneous treatment responses by linking ferroptosis, an iron-dependent cell death pathway, to disease pathogenesis. The resulting gene signature may serve as a potential diagnostic or prognostic biomarker for MPP.

papers.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Prolonged Length of Stay in Older Patients with Lung Cancer: A Multicenter Study Using XGBoost with SHAP Interpretation.
papers.abstract: Prolonged length of stay (PLOS) is common among older patients with lung cancer and is associated with increased risks of adverse outcomes, greater healthcare resource utilization, and reduced treatment efficiency. However, reliable risk stratification tools specifically designed for this population, particularly in the Chinese healthcare context, remain lacking.
papers.summary: This multicenter study developed an XGBoost machine learning model to predict prolonged length of stay (PLOS) in older Chinese patients with lung cancer, using SHAP values to interpret which clinical features drive predictions. The model aims to provide a risk stratification tool tailored to this population and healthcare context, where such tools are currently lacking.

papers.title: Machine learning models for adverse drug reaction prediction. A systematic review and three-level multilevel meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are a leading cause of preventable hospitalization, yet the dominant pharmacovigilance paradigm remains reactive. Machine learning (ML) offers a data-driven alternative, but the evidence base has not been formally meta-analyzed under clinically realistic inclusion criteria and a dependence-respecting statistical framework. This is the first PRISMA 2020-compliant and PROBAST-screened multilevel meta-analysis of broad-spectrum ML-based ADR prediction. We aimed to quantify pooled discrimination of ML models for broad-spectrum ADR prediction and to test the influence
papers.summary: This systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis pools evidence on machine learning models for predicting adverse drug reactions, applying PRISMA 2020 and PROBAST screening criteria. It provides the first formal quantitative synthesis of pooled discrimination performance for broad-spectrum ML-based ADR prediction, while accounting for statistical dependence among model comparisons.

papers.title: AI-assisted crop improvement: new design tools within established regulatory frameworks.
papers.abstract: The integration of Artificial intelligence (AI) into crop improvement offers the potential to enhance the precision, efficiency, and speed of development of new varieties. Accelerated genetic gain is promised by an increasing repertoire of AI tools for analyzing large and complex genetic and phenotypic datasets to discover and elucidate traits and predict functional variants that can be realized with the use of, inter alia, genome editing tools. This power, in combination with parallel AI tool development for optimization of genome editing processes, has generated optimism for a new era of sma
papers.summary: This review discusses how AI tools can accelerate crop improvement by analyzing large genetic and phenotypic datasets to discover traits and predict functional variants, which can then be realized through genome editing. It argues that these AI-assisted approaches can fit within existing regulatory frameworks for genetically modified and edited crops, rather than requiring entirely new oversight systems.

papers.title: Radiomics machine learning model based on multi-sequence MRI for predicting Ki-67 expression level in glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary malignant brain tumor in adults, with median overall survival around 15 months. The Ki- 67 proliferation index is an important marker of proliferative activity and has prognostic relevance in GBM; however, its assessment requires surgical tissue and may be affected by sampling bias. Developing a non-invasive preoperative method to estimate Ki-67 expression may provide adjunctive information for risk assessment, while it should not be regarded as a stand-alone determinant of treatment decisions.
papers.summary: This study developed a radiomics machine learning model using multi-sequence MRI to non-invasively predict Ki-67 proliferation index levels in glioblastoma patients. The approach aims to provide preoperative prognostic information without requiring surgical tissue sampling, potentially reducing sampling bias associated with biopsy-based Ki-67 assessment.

papers.title: Identification and Preliminary mRNA Validation of Key Genes Associated with Tolerogenic Dendritic Cells in Keloid Based on Transcriptome Data.
papers.abstract: Keloid is a cutaneous fibrotic disorder characterized by excessive fibrous tissue proliferation during wound healing. Tolerogenic dendritic cells (tolDCs) may participate in keloid immunopathology, but the related molecular signatures remain unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate tolDC-associated genes in keloid by integrating tolDC-related transcriptomic profiles with keloid transcriptomic datasets.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic profiles of tolerogenic dendritic cells with keloid transcriptome datasets to identify candidate genes linking tolDCs to keloid pathology. The authors then perform preliminary mRNA validation of these key genes, suggesting tolDC-associated molecular signatures may contribute to keloid immunopathology. The work provides early-stage candidate biomarkers but requires further functional validation.

papers.title: Integrative Transcriptomic and Genetic Analyses Identify CDC20 as a Potential Biomarker Associated with Cell Cycle and Immune-Inflammatory Processes in Psoriasis.
papers.abstract: To identify psoriasis-associated candidate genes and regulatory features via integrated transcriptomic, immune and genetic analyses, and validate them in an imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like murine model.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic, immune, and genetic analyses to identify psoriasis-associated candidate genes and regulatory features, pinpointing CDC20 as a potential biomarker linked to cell cycle and immune-inflammatory processes. The findings are validated in an imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like mouse model, supporting CDC20's relevance to disease mechanisms.

papers.title: Metal- and polymer-assisted SEM imaging of protein-bound DNA molecules: a protocol.
papers.abstract: Direct mapping of protein positions along long, stretched DNA molecules requires simultaneous visualization of the DNA backbone and associated protein signals. We recently established a heavy-metal- and polymer-assisted scanning electron microscopy (SEM) approach for imaging stretched DNA molecules and associated protein signals on silicon wafers. Here, we present a practical protocol for implementing this workflow using λ DNA and streptavidin-fluorescent protein-labeled λ DNA as model DNA samples. The protocol encompasses silicon wafer preparation, microchannel-guided DNA deposition, heavy-me
papers.summary: This paper provides a step-by-step protocol for imaging stretched DNA molecules and the proteins bound to them using heavy-metal and polymer-assisted scanning electron microscopy (SEM) on silicon wafers. Using λ DNA and streptavidin-labeled λ DNA as models, the workflow covers wafer preparation, microchannel-guided DNA deposition, and metal staining to visualize both DNA backbones and protein signals simultaneously.

papers.title: AI-driven genotype-phenotype modeling: a framework integrating multi-modal single-cell genomics and reverse vaccinology for de novo design of multi-epitope cancer vaccines.
papers.abstract: Cancer vaccines have emerged as a promising strategy for personalized cancer immunotherapy; however, their development has traditionally relied on bulk sequencing approaches that average molecular information across millions of cells, thereby obscuring the extensive intratumoral heterogeneity that drives disease progression, therapeutic resistance, and immune escape. Recent advances in multi-modal single-cell genomics have transformed the ability to characterize tumors at unprecedented resolution, enabling the identification of distinct cellular populations, clonal evolutionary trajectories, a
papers.summary: This paper proposes an AI-driven framework that combines multi-modal single-cell genomics with reverse vaccinology to design multi-epitope cancer vaccines de novo. It argues that single-cell resolution can capture intratumoral heterogeneity that bulk sequencing misses, enabling more personalized and effective vaccine target selection. The work is a conceptual/methodological framework rather than an experimental validation.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Stem Cell Research: From Biological Data to Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Stem cell (SC) research plays a central role in disease modeling and regenerative medicine, yet its clinical translation remains challenged by biological heterogeneity, incomplete cellular maturation, stringent quality-control requirements, and increasingly complex biological and clinical data. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful computational approach for extracting biologically meaningful information from these data, enabling quantitative characterization of SC behavior and predictive modeling across diverse experimental and translational applications. This review presents a unif
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning is being applied across stem cell research, from analyzing complex biological data to supporting clinical translation. It highlights how ML helps address challenges like cellular heterogeneity, incomplete maturation, and quality control by enabling quantitative characterization and predictive modeling of stem cell behavior.

papers.title: Bio-Inspired Artificial Intelligence Multimorbidity Score for Human-Machine Clinical Risk Stratification.
papers.abstract: Multimorbidity is strongly associated with mortality, but existing comorbidity indices often generalize poorly across populations because they depend on fixed disease lists and context-specific weights. We developed the large-language-model-based multimorbidity score (LLM-MMS), a prompt-based large-language-model-derived multimorbidity phenotype score, as a bio-inspired artificial intelligence score for human-machine clinical risk stratification and evaluated it for all-cause mortality prediction in 770,439 adults from 9 international longitudinal cohorts. Harmonized participant-level data wer
papers.summary: The authors developed LLM-MMS, a prompt-based large language model-derived multimorbidity score designed to predict all-cause mortality across diverse populations. They evaluated it in 770,439 adults from 9 international longitudinal cohorts, aiming to overcome the poor generalizability of fixed disease-list comorbidity indices. The score is framed as a bio-inspired AI tool for human-machine clinical risk stratification.

papers.title: scLTF: A self-training clustering framework for large-scale single-cell RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology has rapidly advanced in recent years, driving significant breakthroughs in developmental biology, cancer research, immunology, and other related fields. However, existing clustering methods still face performance bottlenecks when handling large-scale scRNA-seq data. To address this challenge, we propose a self-training clustering method for large-scale single-cell RNA-seq data, termed scLTF (Single-cell Louvain-Transformer Framework for Large-scale Clustering). This method first generates preliminary clusters using a fast Louvain algorithm and
papers.summary: scLTF is a self-training clustering framework for large-scale scRNA-seq data that combines a fast Louvain algorithm for initial clustering with a Transformer-based model to refine cluster assignments. The approach aims to overcome performance bottlenecks of existing methods when scaling to large single-cell datasets.

papers.title: Architectural good practices for reproducible benchmarking in protein machine learning.
papers.abstract: Reliable benchmarking in protein machine learning requires biological tasks, datasets, representations, execution conditions, and evaluation regimes to be explicitly defined and traceable. Protein-specific dependencies, including label semantics, negative-class construction, evolutionary relationships, similarity control, inferred structures, protein language model configurations, and potential pretraining contamination, can alter benchmark interpretation. This Perspective provides an operational, protein-specific synthesis of established reproducibility practices through an artefact-linked ar
papers.summary: This perspective article synthesizes reproducibility best practices specifically for protein machine learning benchmarking, emphasizing that biological tasks, datasets, representations, execution conditions, and evaluation regimes must be explicitly defined and traceable. It highlights protein-specific pitfalls such as label semantics, negative-class construction, evolutionary relationships, similarity control, inferred structures, protein language model configurations, and pretraining contamination that can distort benchmark interpretation.

papers.title: A trainable language model with potential to modulate translation rates in non-model organisms by generating upstream untranslated region sequence libraries.
papers.abstract: Tuning protein expression in non-model organisms is often constrained by the lack of validated genetic parts and predictive design tools. Translational tuning through the modulation of upstream untranslated regions (5'-UTRs) offers a potentially organism-agnostic route, but existing methods typically rely on mechanistic assumptions, prior knowledge that may not be available in non-model contexts, or the screening of sequence libraries. Here, we present a simple generative approach for creating synthetic 5'-UTR libraries based solely on the genomic sequence statistics of any desired organism. T
papers.summary: The authors present a trainable language model that generates synthetic 5'-UTR sequence libraries using only the genomic sequence statistics of a target organism, without requiring prior mechanistic knowledge or validated genetic parts. This approach aims to enable translational tuning in non-model organisms by providing an organism-agnostic route to modulate protein expression.
